title: Where the Tool Points: Position and Heading of a Three-Link Arm, and the Target That Is Reachable as a Point and Not as a Pose

questions.question: Headings 3.14 and -3.14. What is their difference the short way round?
questions.explanation: The difference of the numbers is 6.28 and the short way round is -0.00318531.

questions.question: Why is the heading of a three link arm the sum of its angles?
options: Each angle is measured from the link before it, so the directions add
questions.explanation: A heading of 2 pi after folding out, back and out.

questions.question: A point is inside the total reach of the arm. Can every heading be reached there?
options: No: the wrist, the tool less the last link, has to be within reach of the first two
questions.explanation: (2.9, 0) was reachable along x and not back along it.

questions.question: What has to be within reach for a pose, the tool or the wrist?
options: The wrist: it is what the first two links reach
questions.explanation: The test of a pose is the test of the wrist.

questions.question: How many whole-degree headings could be reached at (1.5, 0) with links 1, 1, 1?
questions.explanation: The wrist must be within 2 of the base: cos(phi) at least -0.25.

questions.question: What does the third angle of a solution do?
options: Turns the heading into the one that was asked for
